title: Remove the engine from the frame and refit it
completeness: Covers draining, bodywork, air filter case, shock and linkage release for exhaust access, exhaust, throttle body, cooling hoses, wiring, clutch cable, sprocket and chain, mounts, lifting the engine out to the right and the full refit with every torque. Engine internals are in the top end and bottom end guides.

required_tools.name: Frame stand and a swingarm support
Engine jack or blocks and a helper
Sprocket holder or a helper on the rear brake

required_parts.name: Exhaust gaskets (3)
required_parts.purpose: Renewed whenever the exhaust is apart.

prerequisites: Rebuild record available if the engine was opened.
critical_stop_conditions: Bike or engine unstable on its supports: stop and re-support.
A lead, hose or cable still attached as the engine moves: stop.
Damaged threads or cracked mounts: stop and repair before refitting.
Pivot shaft bent: replace, do not straighten.
Never open the radiator cap hot.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Note why the engine is coming out and how it ran. Photograph the hose, wiring and cable routing on both sides before anything is disconnected.

steps.title: Drain the engine oil
steps.instruction: With the bike upright on level ground, remove the oil filler cap and the drain bolt and let the oil drain fully. Refit the drain bolt with a new gasket at 20 N·m (15 lb·ft).
verification: Oil drained, drain bolt refitted with a new gasket.

steps.title: Drain the coolant
steps.instruction: Engine cold. Put a pan close under the coolant drain bolt. Remove the drain bolt and its copper washer. Lay a thick rag over the radiator cap, turn it slowly to the first stop until any hiss stops, then press and remove it. When drained, refit the drain bolt with a new copper washer at 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: Coolant drained, drain bolt refitted with a new washer.

steps.title: Support the bike
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the frame so it stays steady with the engine out. Have a second support ready for the swingarm.

steps.title: Take off the seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Remove the side cover bolts and pull both side covers off, then remove the seat bolts and slide the seat back and off. Keep each bolt with its part.
verification: Seat and both side covers off, bolts bagged by part.

steps.title: Take off the air scoops
steps.instruction: Remove the bolts holding each of the air scoops to the frame, radiator guard and tank, and lift both off without bending the plastic tabs.

steps.title: Empty the tank and unplug the fuel line
steps.instruction: Pump the fuel out through the filler. Lay a rag under and over the fuel hose joint first, because the line holds pressure and can spray. Release the hose connector by hand only (slide the holder and cover, press the two side buttons) and never lever it with tools. Unplug the fuel pump connector. Cap the open hose and the pump fitting so no dirt gets in.
verification: Tank drained, fuel hose and pump connector off, both open ends capped.

steps.title: Lift the tank off
steps.instruction: Remove the tank bolts and lift the tank away. Lean it against a wall or prop it on its side; never stand it on the fuel pump face.
verification: Tank off and stored resting off the pump face.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Disconnect the negative battery lead first, then the positive, and cover the terminals.

steps.title: Remove the air filter case
steps.instruction: Take off the air filter case cover. Remove the ECU (two bolts) and the ignition coil (two bolts) from the case and move them aside on their wiring. Unplug the intake air temperature sensor connector. Loosen the air filter case joint clamp screw, remove the three case bolts and lift the case out. Cover the throttle body inlet.
verification: Air filter case out, ECU and coil moved aside, intake covered.

steps.title: Free the rear shock for exhaust access
steps.instruction: Support the swingarm, then remove the shock lower bolt and bolt and the connecting arm bolt on the frame side so the shock can be moved to the left.
verification: Shock lower mount and connecting arm frame bolt out, swingarm supported.

steps.title: Remove the exhaust
steps.instruction: Take off the right side cover if still fitted. Loosen the silencer clamp, remove the silencer bolts and pull the silencer off. Loosen the clamp on exhaust pipe 2, remove its bracket bolt and work pipe 2 out. Remove the header nuts and header pipe 1. Discard all three exhaust gaskets.

steps.title: Free the throttle body
steps.instruction: Unplug the injector, intake air pressure sensor and throttle position sensor connectors. Loosen the throttle body joint clamp screw on the engine side and pull the throttle body back out of the joint with the cables still attached; tie it clear without kinking them, and cover the engine intake. If the cables are under strain, take them off at the throttle body instead.
verification: Throttle body clear; both openings covered.

steps.title: Disconnect the coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Mark the radiator hoses and clamp positions at the engine, loosen the engine-side clamps and pull the hoses off. Cover the open ports.
verification: Engine coolant hoses off and marked.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine wiring
steps.instruction: Remove the rectifier/regulator (two bolts). Unplug the AC magneto connector, the crankshaft position sensor connector, the coolant temperature sensor connector and the gear position switch connector, and remove the condenser. Pull off the spark plug cap. At the starter motor, hold the inner nut with a spanner while undoing the starter lead nut. Release the clamps and ties holding these leads and label everything.
verification: All engine leads unplugged, labelled and clear.

steps.title: Disconnect the clutch cable
steps.instruction: Give the cable full slack at the lever adjuster, loosen the cable locknuts at the engine and unhook the cable from the clutch push lever.

steps.title: Remove sprocket cover, chain and drive sprocket
steps.instruction: Remove the drive sprocket cover and chain guide. Straighten the lock washer and loosen the sprocket nut while a helper holds the rear brake on. Remove the nut and lock washer and take the sprocket off together with the chain. Mark the shift pedal against the punch mark on the shaft and remove it.
verification: Sprocket, chain and shift pedal off the engine.

steps.title: Remove the engine guard, brake pedal and breather
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard. Remove the brake pedal bolt and spring, leaving the pedal on the master cylinder. Release the cylinder head breather hose.
verification: Guard, pedal bolt and spring off; breather free.

steps.title: Support engine and swingarm
steps.instruction: Put a jack or block under the engine so it is carried, not hanging. Keep the swingarm supported. Check every hose, lead and cable is free of the engine.
verification: Engine and swingarm supported; nothing still attached.

steps.title: Remove the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Remove the right and left upper engine brackets and the two lower brackets with their bolts. Pull the swingarm pivot shaft; if possible push a bar of the same diameter in from the other side so the swingarm stays located.
verification: Brackets off, pivot shaft out, swingarm supported.

steps.title: Lift the engine out
steps.instruction: With a helper, lift the engine and swing its bottom out to the right side of the frame. Stop if anything catches. Set it on a clean bench support and cover every opening.

steps.title: Check the mounts before refitting
steps.instruction: Inspect brackets, bolts and pivot shaft. Roll the pivot shaft on a flat surface; a bent shaft is replaced. If the engine was rebuilt, confirm the rebuild is complete and recorded.
verification: Mount hardware inspected; rebuild record confirmed.

steps.title: Put the engine back in
steps.instruction: Lift the engine in from the right side without trapping any lead or hose. Grease the pivot shaft with molybdenum disulfide grease and fit it.
verification: Engine in place, pivot shaft through.

steps.title: Torque the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Fit the brackets and bolts in their original places. Tighten: pivot shaft nut 85 N·m (63 lb·ft), lower engine mounting bolt 53 N·m (39 lb·ft), front engine bracket bolts 34 N·m (25 lb·ft), front engine mounting bolt 53 N·m (39 lb·ft), upper engine bracket bolts 34 N·m (25 lb·ft), upper engine mounting bolt 45 N·m (33 lb·ft).
verification: Every mount fastener torqued and marked.

steps.title: Refit pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Fit the spring, the brake pedal with new O-rings and the pivot bolt, greased with lithium-soap grease; tighten the bolt to 26 N·m (19 lb·ft) and fit the clip. Refit the engine guard at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and route the breather hose as it came off.
verification: Pedal 26 N·m, guard 7 N·m, breather routed.

steps.title: Refit sprocket, chain and covers
steps.instruction: Fit the drive sprocket together with the chain, a new lock washer and the nut. Tighten the nut to 75 N·m (55 lb·ft) while a helper holds the rear brake on, then bend the lock washer against a flat. Refit the chain guide and sprocket cover at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Line up the punch marks and tighten the shift pedal bolt to 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft).
verification: Sprocket nut torqued and locked; cover 7 N·m; pedal 12 N·m.

steps.title: Reconnect the clutch cable
steps.instruction: Hook the cable onto the push lever, tighten the engine-side cable locknut to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft), then set free play at the lever to 7.0–12.0 mm (0.28–0.47 in) and tighten the lever-side locknut to 4.3 N·m (3.2 lb·ft).
verification: Clutch free play 7-12 mm; locknuts torqued.

steps.title: Reconnect the engine wiring
steps.instruction: Refit the starter lead nut at 6 N·m (4.4 lb·ft) holding the inner nut. Reconnect every connector you unplugged, refit the condenser and the rectifier/regulator at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft), push the plug cap fully home and restore the clamps and ties as in your photos.
verification: All connectors home; rectifier 7 N·m; starter lead 6 N·m.

steps.title: Reconnect the coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Push the hoses fully onto their engine stubs in the marked positions and tighten the clamp screws to 1.5 N·m (1.1 lb·ft).

steps.title: Refit the throttle body
steps.instruction: Uncover the intake, seat the throttle body fully in its joint and tighten the joint clamp screw to 3.0 N·m (2.2 lb·ft). Reconnect the three sensor connectors. Check the throttle opens fully and snaps shut with the bars turned both ways.

steps.title: Refit the exhaust
steps.instruction: Fit a new header gasket and header pipe 1; run the nuts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) first, then 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Fit new joint gaskets, pipe 2 with its clamp and bracket bolt, then the silencer and its clamp; clamp tabs in the slots, not on the raised lips. Silencer bolts 30 N·m (22 lb·ft), pipe 2 bracket bolt 20 N·m (15 lb·ft), both clamps 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft).
verification: Header 7 then 10 N·m; silencer 30; bracket 20; clamps 12 N·m.

steps.title: Reconnect the shock and connecting arm
steps.instruction: Grease the bolts with molybdenum disulfide grease, lift the swingarm and refit the connecting arm bolt on the frame side (from the right) and the shock lower bolt (from the left). Tighten the connecting arm bolt (frame side) to 80 N·m (59 lb·ft) and the shock lower bolt to 53 N·m (39 lb·ft).
verification: Connecting arm 80 N·m; shock lower 53 N·m.

steps.title: Refit the air filter case
steps.instruction: Seat the case on the throttle body with the joint lip even, tighten the three case bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and the joint clamp screw to 3.0 N·m (2.2 lb·ft). Refit the ignition coil at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and the ECU at 3.8 N·m (2.8 lb·ft). Plug in the air temperature sensor and refit the cover.
verification: Case 7 N·m; clamp 3.0 N·m; coil 7 N·m; ECU 3.8 N·m.

steps.title: Reconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Connect the positive lead first, then the negative.

steps.title: Refit the tank and reconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Set the tank on the frame without trapping any wires or hoses and tighten the front bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and the rear bolt to 9 N·m (6.6 lb·ft). Remove the caps and push the fuel hose onto the pump fitting until it clicks, slide the connector cover back and fit the holder the right way round. Reconnect the fuel pump connector. Make sure the hose is not kinked or pinched.
verification: Fuel hose clicked home, holder fitted, pump connector plugged in.

steps.title: Refit the air scoops, seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Fit both air scoops and tighten their bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Fit the seat, engaging its front hook first, and tighten the seat bolts to 22 N·m (16 lb·ft). Fit the side covers and tighten the side cover bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
verification: All panels on and torqued; seat does not move.

steps.title: Check for fuel leaks
steps.instruction: Refuel with fresh fuel. With the engine running at idle, look and smell around the hose joint and the pump flange for any leak, then stop the engine.
verification: No fuel leak at the hose joint or pump.

steps.title: Fill the coolant
steps.instruction: Fill with a 1:1 mix of ethylene-glycol antifreeze made for aluminium engines and distilled water; the full system takes about 1.03 L (1.09 US qt). Fill to the top, refit the cap, run the engine a few minutes, let it cool and top up again.
verification: System full after warm-up and cool-down.

steps.title: Fill the oil
steps.instruction: Add 0.90 L (0.95 US qt) after a full rebuild (less after only an oil or filter change; see the break-in guide). Refit the filler cap.

steps.title: Set chain slack
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel off the ground and the gearbox in neutral, set slack to 50–60 mm (1.97–2.36 in) with both adjusters equal. Tighten the rear axle nut to 134 N·m (100 lb·ft) and the adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft).
verification: Slack in range; axle and locknuts torqued.

steps.title: Go to the first-start guide
steps.instruction: Follow the first start and break-in guide for this bike for the oil circulation check, leak checks and break-in.

steps.instruction: With the bike upright on level ground, remove the oil filler cap and the drain bolt and let the oil drain fully. Refit the drain bolt with a new gasket at 20 N·m (15 lb·ft).
verification: Oil drained, drain bolt refitted with a new gasket.

steps.title: Drain the coolant
steps.instruction: Engine cold. Put a pan close under the coolant drain bolt. Remove the drain bolt and its copper washer. Lay a thick rag over the radiator cap, turn it slowly to the first stop until any hiss stops, then press and remove it. When drained, refit the drain bolt with a new copper washer at 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: Coolant drained, drain bolt refitted with a new washer.

steps.title: Support the bike
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the frame so it stays steady with the engine out. Have a second support ready for the swingarm.

steps.title: Take off the seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Remove the side cover bolts and pull both side covers off, then remove the seat bolts and slide the seat back and off. Keep each bolt with its part.
verification: Seat and both side covers off, bolts bagged by part.

steps.title: Take off the air scoops
steps.instruction: Remove the bolts holding each of the air scoops to the frame, radiator guard and tank, and lift both off without bending the plastic tabs.

steps.title: Empty the tank and unplug the fuel line
steps.instruction: Pump the fuel out through the filler. Lay a rag under and over the fuel hose joint first, because the line holds pressure and can spray. Release the hose connector by hand only (slide the holder and cover, press the two side buttons) and never lever it with tools. Unplug the fuel pump connector. Cap the open hose and the pump fitting so no dirt gets in.
verification: Tank drained, fuel hose and pump connector off, both open ends capped.

steps.title: Lift the tank off
steps.instruction: Remove the tank bolts and lift the tank away. Lean it against a wall or prop it on its side; never stand it on the fuel pump face.
verification: Tank off and stored resting off the pump face.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Disconnect the negative battery lead first, then the positive, and cover the terminals.

steps.title: Remove the air filter case
steps.instruction: Take off the air filter case cover. Remove the ECU (two bolts) and the ignition coil (two bolts) from the case and move them aside on their wiring. Unplug the intake air temperature sensor connector. Loosen the air filter case joint clamp screw, remove the three case bolts and lift the case out. Cover the throttle body inlet.
verification: Air filter case out, ECU and coil moved aside, intake covered.

steps.title: Free the rear shock for exhaust access
steps.instruction: Support the swingarm, then remove the shock lower nut and bolt and the connecting arm bolt on the frame side so the shock can be moved to the left.
verification: Shock lower mount and connecting arm frame bolt out, swingarm supported.

steps.title: Remove the exhaust
steps.instruction: Take off the right side cover if still fitted. Loosen the silencer clamp, remove the silencer bolts and pull the silencer off. Loosen the clamp on exhaust pipe 2, remove its bracket bolt and work pipe 2 out. Remove the header nuts and header pipe 1. Discard all three exhaust gaskets.

steps.title: Free the throttle body
steps.instruction: Unplug the injector, intake air pressure sensor and throttle position sensor connectors. Loosen the throttle body joint clamp screw on the engine side and pull the throttle body back out of the joint with the cables still attached; tie it clear without kinking them, and cover the engine intake. If the cables are under strain, take them off at the throttle body instead.
verification: Throttle body clear; both openings covered.

steps.title: Disconnect the coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Mark the radiator hoses and clamp positions at the engine, loosen the engine-side clamps and pull the hoses off. Cover the open ports.
verification: Engine coolant hoses off and marked.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine wiring
steps.instruction: Remove the rectifier/regulator (two bolts). Unplug the stator coil connector, the crankshaft position sensor connector, the coolant temperature sensor connector and the gear position switch connector. Pull off the spark plug cap. At the starter motor, hold the inner nut with a spanner while undoing the starter lead nut. Release the clamps and ties holding these leads and label everything.
verification: All engine leads unplugged, labelled and clear.

steps.title: Disconnect the clutch cable
steps.instruction: Give the cable full slack at the lever adjuster, loosen the cable locknuts at the engine and unhook the cable from the clutch push lever.

steps.title: Remove sprocket cover, chain and drive sprocket
steps.instruction: Remove the drive sprocket cover and chain guide. Remove the master link clip, link and plate and take the chain off. Flatten the lock washer, hold the sprocket and remove the sprocket nut, lock washer and sprocket. Mark the shift pedal against the punch mark on the shaft and remove it.
verification: Sprocket, chain and shift pedal off the engine.

steps.title: Remove the engine guard, brake pedal and breather
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard. Remove the brake pedal bolt and spring, leaving the pedal on the master cylinder. Release the cylinder head breather hose.
verification: Guard, pedal bolt and spring off; breather free.

steps.title: Support engine and swingarm
steps.instruction: Put a jack or block under the engine so it is carried, not hanging. Keep the swingarm supported. Check every hose, lead and cable is free of the engine.
verification: Engine and swingarm supported; nothing still attached.

steps.title: Remove the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Remove the right and left upper engine brackets and the two lower brackets with their bolts. Keep the four bracket shims with their brackets. Pull the swingarm pivot shaft; if possible push a bar of the same diameter in from the other side so the swingarm stays located.
verification: Brackets off, pivot shaft out, swingarm supported.

steps.title: Lift the engine out
steps.instruction: With a helper, lift the engine and swing its bottom out to the right side of the frame. Stop if anything catches. Set it on a clean bench support and cover every opening.

steps.title: Check the mounts before refitting
steps.instruction: Inspect brackets, bolts and pivot shaft. Roll the pivot shaft on a flat surface; a bent shaft is replaced. If the engine was rebuilt, confirm the rebuild is complete and recorded.
verification: Mount hardware inspected; rebuild record confirmed.

steps.title: Put the engine back in
steps.instruction: Lift the engine in from the right side without trapping any lead or hose. Grease the pivot shaft with molybdenum disulfide grease and fit it.
verification: Engine in place, pivot shaft through.

steps.title: Torque the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Fit the brackets and bolts in their original places. Fit the shims with their projections facing out from the bike. Tighten: pivot shaft nut 85 N·m (63 lb·ft), lower engine mounting bolt 53 N·m (39 lb·ft), front engine bracket bolts 34 N·m (25 lb·ft), front engine mounting bolt 55 N·m (41 lb·ft), upper engine bracket bolts 34 N·m (25 lb·ft), upper engine mounting bolt 45 N·m (33 lb·ft).
verification: Every mount fastener torqued and marked.

steps.title: Refit pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Fit the spring and brake pedal, grease the pivot with lithium-soap grease and tighten the pedal bolt to 26 N·m (19 lb·ft). Refit the engine guard at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and route the breather hose as it came off.
verification: Pedal 26 N·m, guard 7 N·m, breather routed.

steps.title: Refit sprocket, chain and covers
steps.instruction: Fit the drive sprocket, a new lock washer and the nut; tighten the nut to 90 N·m (66 lb·ft) and bend the lock washer against a flat. Fit the chain with the master link and a clip whose closed end faces the direction of chain travel. Refit the chain guide and sprocket cover at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Line up the punch marks and tighten the shift pedal bolt to 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft).
verification: Sprocket nut torqued and locked; cover 7 N·m; pedal 12 N·m.

steps.title: Reconnect the clutch cable
steps.instruction: Hook the cable onto the push lever, tighten the engine-side cable locknut to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft), then set free play at the lever to 7.0–12.0 mm (0.28–0.47 in) and tighten the lever-side locknut to 4.3 N·m (3.2 lb·ft).
verification: Clutch free play 7-12 mm; locknuts torqued.

steps.title: Reconnect the engine wiring
steps.instruction: Refit the starter lead nut at 6 N·m (4.4 lb·ft) holding the inner nut. Reconnect every connector you unplugged, refit the rectifier/regulator at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft), push the plug cap fully home and restore the clamps and ties as in your photos.
verification: All connectors home; rectifier 7 N·m; starter lead 6 N·m.

steps.title: Reconnect the coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Push the hoses fully onto their engine stubs in the marked positions and tighten the clamp screws to 1.5 N·m (1.1 lb·ft).

steps.title: Refit the throttle body
steps.instruction: Uncover the intake, seat the throttle body fully in its joint and tighten the joint clamp screw to 3.0 N·m (2.2 lb·ft). Reconnect the three sensor connectors. Check the throttle opens fully and snaps shut with the bars turned both ways.

steps.title: Refit the exhaust
steps.instruction: Fit a new header gasket and header pipe 1; run the nuts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) first, then 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Fit new joint gaskets, pipe 2 with its clamp and bracket bolt, then the silencer and its clamp; clamp tabs in the slots, not on the raised lips. Silencer bolts 30 N·m (22 lb·ft), pipe 2 bracket bolt 20 N·m (15 lb·ft), both clamps 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft).
verification: Header 7 then 10 N·m; silencer 30; bracket 20; clamps 12 N·m.

steps.title: Reconnect the shock and connecting arm
steps.instruction: Grease the bolts with molybdenum disulfide grease, lift the swingarm and refit the connecting arm bolt on the frame side (from the right) and the shock lower bolt (from the left). Tighten the connecting arm nut (frame side) to 80 N·m (59 lb·ft) and the shock lower nut to 53 N·m (39 lb·ft).
verification: Connecting arm 80 N·m; shock lower 53 N·m.

steps.title: Refit the air filter case
steps.instruction: Seat the case on the throttle body with the joint lip even, tighten the three case bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and the joint clamp screw to 3.0 N·m (2.2 lb·ft). Refit the ignition coil at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and the ECU at 3.8 N·m (2.8 lb·ft). Plug in the air temperature sensor and refit the cover.
verification: Case 7 N·m; clamp 3.0 N·m; coil 7 N·m; ECU 3.8 N·m.

steps.title: Reconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Connect the positive lead first, then the negative.

steps.title: Refit the tank and reconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Set the tank on the frame without trapping any wires or hoses and tighten the front bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and the rear bolt to 9 N·m (6.6 lb·ft). Remove the caps and push the fuel hose onto the pump fitting until it clicks, slide the connector cover back and fit the holder the right way round. Reconnect the fuel pump connector. Make sure the hose is not kinked or pinched.
verification: Fuel hose clicked home, holder fitted, pump connector plugged in.

steps.title: Refit the air scoops, seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Fit both air scoops and tighten their bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Fit the seat, engaging its front hook first, and tighten the seat bolts to 22 N·m (16 lb·ft). Fit the side covers and tighten the side cover bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
verification: All panels on and torqued; seat does not move.

steps.title: Check for fuel leaks
steps.instruction: Refuel with fresh fuel. With the engine running at idle, look and smell around the hose joint and the pump flange for any leak, then stop the engine.
verification: No fuel leak at the hose joint or pump.

steps.title: Fill the coolant
steps.instruction: Fill with a 1:1 mix of ethylene-glycol antifreeze made for aluminium engines and distilled water; the full system takes about 1.03 L (1.09 US qt). Fill to the top, refit the cap, run the engine a few minutes, let it cool and top up again.
verification: System full after warm-up and cool-down.

steps.title: Fill the oil
steps.instruction: Add 0.90 L (0.95 US qt) after a full rebuild (less after only an oil or filter change; see the break-in guide). Refit the filler cap.

steps.title: Set chain slack
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel off the ground and the gearbox in neutral, set slack to 50–60 mm (1.97–2.36 in) with both adjusters equal. Tighten the rear axle nut to 135 N·m (100 lb·ft) and the adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft).
verification: Slack in range; axle and locknuts torqued.

steps.title: Go to the first-start guide
steps.instruction: Follow the first start and break-in guide for this bike for the oil circulation check, leak checks and break-in.

entry_state: Bike cold, washed, on level ground.
exit_state: Engine refitted with every mount, hose, lead and cable restored and torqued, fluids filled, ready for the first-start guide.
title: Remove the engine from the frame and refit it
completeness: Covers draining, bodywork, intake, exhaust, cooling, wiring, chain and sprocket, clutch release and mount removal, lifting the engine out to the right, and the full refit with every torque. Engine internals are in the top end and bottom end guides.

required_tools.name: Frame stand and a second support for the swingarm
Engine jack or blocks and a helper
Molybdenum disulfide grease, lithium-soap grease, silicone grease, threadlocker

required_parts.name: Oil drain bolt gaskets (2) and filler cap O-ring
Exhaust gaskets (3)
required_parts.purpose: Renewed whenever the exhaust is taken apart.

prerequisites: Rebuild record available if the engine was opened.
critical_stop_conditions: Bike or engine unstable on its supports: stop and re-support before going on.
A lead, hose or cable still attached as the engine moves: stop.
Damaged threads or cracked mounts on the frame or engine: stop and repair before refitting.
Pivot shaft bent: replace, do not straighten.
Never open the radiator cap hot.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Note why the engine is coming out and how it ran. Photograph the hose, wiring and cable routing on both sides before anything is disconnected; the routing has to go back exactly as it was.

steps.title: Drain the engine oil
steps.instruction: With the bike upright on level ground, remove the oil filler cap, the crankcase drain bolt and the oil tank drain bolt and let both drain fully. Refit both drain bolts with new gaskets: crankcase 20 N·m (15 lb·ft), oil tank 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: Oil drained, drain bolts refitted with new gaskets.

steps.title: Drain the coolant
steps.instruction: Engine cold. Put a pan close under the coolant drain bolt (the coolant can shoot out sideways). Remove the drain bolt and its copper washer. Lay a thick rag over the radiator cap, turn it slowly to the first stop until any hiss stops, then press and remove it. When drained, refit the drain bolt with a new copper washer at 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: Coolant drained, drain bolt refitted with new washer.

steps.title: Support the bike
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand under the frame so it stays steady with the engine out. Have a second support ready for the swingarm.

steps.title: Take off the seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Remove the side cover bolts and pull both side covers off, then remove the seat bolts and slide the seat back and off. Keep each bolt with its part.
verification: Seat and both side covers off, bolts bagged by part.

steps.title: Take off the shrouds
steps.instruction: Remove the bolts holding each of the shrouds to the frame, radiator guard and tank, and lift both off without bending the plastic tabs.

steps.title: Empty the tank and unplug the fuel line
steps.instruction: Pump the fuel out through the filler. Lay a rag under and over the fuel hose joint first, because the line holds pressure and can spray. Release the hose connector by hand only (slide the holder and cover, press the two side buttons) and never lever it with tools. Unplug the fuel pump connector. Cap the open hose and the pump fitting so no dirt gets in.
verification: Tank drained, fuel hose and pump connector off, both open ends capped.

steps.title: Lift the tank off
steps.instruction: Remove the tank bolts and lift the tank away. Lean it against a wall or prop it on its side; never stand it on the fuel pump face.
verification: Tank off and stored resting off the pump face.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Disconnect the negative battery lead first, then the positive, and cover the terminals so nothing can touch them.

steps.title: Remove the air filter case
steps.instruction: Take off the air filter case cover. Unplug the intake air temperature sensor connector. Loosen the air filter case joint clamp screw and remove the three case bolts, keeping their collars and dampers in order. Lift the case off the throttle body and cover the throttle body inlet.
verification: Air filter case off, intake covered.

steps.title: Remove the exhaust
steps.instruction: Take off the right side cover if still fitted. Loosen the silencer clamp, remove the two silencer bolts and pull the silencer off. Loosen the clamp on exhaust pipe 2, remove the exhaust pipe bracket bolt and work pipe 2 out. Remove the header nuts and header pipe 1 and discard the three exhaust gaskets.
verification: Silencer and both pipes off, old gaskets discarded.

steps.title: Free the throttle body
steps.instruction: Clean around the throttle body joint. Loosen the throttle body joint clamp screw on the engine side and pull the throttle body back out of the joint. Leave the throttle cables connected, tie the throttle body clear of the engine without kinking the cables, and cover the engine intake. If the cables are under strain, take them off at the throttle body instead.
verification: Throttle body clear and both openings covered.

steps.title: Disconnect the coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Mark radiator hoses 1, 3 and 4 and their clamp positions, loosen the engine-side clamps and pull the hoses off the engine. Plug or cover the open ports.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine wiring
steps.instruction: Unplug the stator coil connector, the crankshaft position sensor connector, the gear position switch connector and the coolant temperature sensor connector. Pull off the spark plug cap. Remove the engine ground terminal bolt. At the starter motor, hold the inner nut with a spanner while undoing the starter lead nut. Release the clamps and ties that hold these leads to the engine and label everything.
verification: All engine leads unplugged, labelled and moved clear.

steps.title: Remove the chain, drive sprocket and shift pedal
steps.instruction: Remove the drive sprocket cover. Remove the master link clip, master link and plate and take the chain off. Flatten the lock washer, hold the sprocket and remove the sprocket nut, lock washer and sprocket. Mark the shift pedal against the punch mark on the shaft and remove it.
verification: Chain, sprocket and shift pedal off.

steps.title: Unbolt the clutch release cylinder
steps.instruction: Remove the two clutch release cylinder bolts and pull the cylinder off with its hose still connected. Keep the washer. Tie it clear without stretching the hose and do not pull the clutch lever while it is off. Push rod 2 stays in the engine.
verification: Release cylinder off and hanging free, hose intact.

steps.title: Remove the engine guard, brake pedal and breather
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard. Remove the brake pedal bolt and spring, leaving the pedal attached to the master cylinder. Release the cylinder head breather hose from the engine and its holder.
verification: Guard, pedal bolt and spring off; breather free.

steps.title: Support engine and swingarm
steps.instruction: Put a jack or block under the engine so it is carried, not hanging. Support the swingarm. Check that every hose, lead and cable is free of the engine before touching the mounts.
verification: Engine and swingarm both supported; nothing still attached.

steps.title: Remove the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Remove the right and left upper engine brackets and the two lower engine brackets with their bolts, keeping each set together. Pull the swingarm pivot shaft. If possible push a bar of the same diameter in from the other side as it comes out so the swingarm stays located.
verification: Brackets off, pivot shaft out, swingarm still supported.

steps.title: Lift the engine out
steps.instruction: With a helper, lift the engine and swing its bottom out to the right side of the frame. Stop if anything catches. Set it on a clean bench support and cover every opening.
verification: Engine out and supported on the bench.

steps.title: Check the mounts before refitting
steps.instruction: Inspect the brackets, mount bolts and pivot shaft for bends, wear or cracks. Roll the pivot shaft on a flat surface; a bent shaft is replaced. If the engine was rebuilt, confirm that rebuild is complete and recorded before it goes back in.
verification: Mount hardware inspected; rebuild record confirmed.

steps.title: Put the engine back in
steps.instruction: Lift the engine in from the right side, bottom first, without trapping any lead or hose. Grease the pivot shaft with molybdenum disulfide grease and push it in from the right. Put lithium-soap grease on the pivot nut threads and face.
verification: Engine in place, pivot shaft through from the right.

steps.title: Torque the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Fit the brackets and bolts in their original places, then tighten: pivot shaft nut 75 N·m (55 lb·ft), lower engine mounting bolt 53 N·m (39 lb·ft), front engine bracket bolts 34 N·m (25 lb·ft), front engine mounting bolt 55 N·m (41 lb·ft), upper engine bracket bolts 34 N·m (25 lb·ft), upper engine mounting bolt 45 N·m (33 lb·ft).
verification: Every mount fastener torqued and marked.

steps.title: Refit the clutch release cylinder
steps.instruction: Fit a new O-ring and put silicone grease on it, the seal lip and the push rod end. Refit the washer and the release cylinder. Put threadlocker on the two bolts and tighten them to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: Release cylinder bolts 10 N·m with threadlocker.

steps.title: Refit pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Grease the brake pedal pivot, refit the spring and tighten the brake pedal bolt to 26 N·m (19 lb·ft). Refit the engine guard at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Route the breather hose between the two front bracket bolts and the rear bracket bolt with its paint mark inside the holder.
verification: Pedal 26 N·m, guard 7 N·m, breather routed.

steps.title: Refit sprocket, pedal and chain
steps.instruction: Fit the drive sprocket with a new lock washer. Put threadlocker on the sprocket nut, tighten it to 90 N·m (66 lb·ft) and bend the lock washer against a flat. Line up the punch marks and tighten the shift pedal bolt to 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft). Refit the sprocket cover at 6 N·m (4.4 lb·ft). Fit the chain with the master link and plate and a clip whose closed end faces the direction of chain travel.
verification: Sprocket nut 90 N·m and locked; chain clip the right way round.

steps.title: Reconnect the engine wiring
steps.instruction: Refit the engine ground terminal at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Refit the starter lead nut at 6 N·m (4.4 lb·ft) while holding the inner nut. Reconnect the stator, crankshaft position, gear position and coolant temperature connectors and their covers, push the spark plug cap fully home and restore every clamp and tie as in your photos.
verification: All connectors home; ground 7 N·m; starter lead 6 N·m.

steps.title: Reconnect the coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Push radiator hoses 1, 3 and 4 fully onto their engine stubs in the marked positions and tighten the clamp screws to 1.5 N·m (1.1 lb·ft). Check no hose is kinked.

steps.title: Refit the throttle body
steps.instruction: Uncover the intake and seat the throttle body fully in its joint. Tighten the joint clamp screw to 3.0 N·m (2.2 lb·ft). Check the throttle opens fully and snaps shut with the bars turned both ways.

steps.title: Refit the exhaust
steps.instruction: Fit a new header gasket and header pipe 1. Run all header nuts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) first, then to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Fit new joint gaskets, pipe 2 with its clamp and the bracket bolt, then the silencer and clamp; the clamp tabs must sit in the slots, not on the raised lips. Tighten the silencer bolts to 30 N·m (22 lb·ft), the exhaust bracket bolt to 20 N·m (15 lb·ft) and both exhaust clamp bolts to 16 N·m (12 lb·ft).
verification: Header 7 then 10 N·m; silencer 30; bracket 20; clamps 16 N·m.

steps.title: Refit the air filter case
steps.instruction: Uncover the throttle body inlet, seat the case on it with the joint lip even all round, fit the collars and dampers and tighten the three case bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and the joint clamp screw to 3.0 N·m (2.2 lb·ft). Plug in the air temperature sensor. Refit the cover.
verification: Case bolts 7 N·m, clamp 3.0 N·m, sensor plugged in.

steps.title: Reconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Connect the positive lead first, then the negative, and refit the terminal cover.

steps.title: Refit the tank and reconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Set the tank on the frame without trapping any wires or hoses and tighten the front bolts to 8 N·m (5.9 lb·ft) and the tank screw to 4.0 N·m (3.0 lb·ft). Remove the caps and push the fuel hose onto the pump fitting until it clicks, slide the connector cover back and fit the holder the right way round. Reconnect the fuel pump connector. Make sure the hose is not kinked or pinched.
verification: Fuel hose clicked home, holder fitted, pump connector plugged in.

steps.title: Refit the shrouds, seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Fit both shrouds and tighten their bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Fit the seat, engaging its front hook first, and tighten the seat bolts to 13 N·m (9.6 lb·ft). Fit the side covers and tighten the side cover bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and the centre side cover bolts to 9.5 N·m (7.0 lb·ft).
verification: All panels on and torqued; seat does not move.

steps.title: Check for fuel leaks
steps.instruction: Refuel with fresh fuel. With the engine running at idle, look and smell around the hose joint and the pump flange for any leak, then stop the engine.
verification: No fuel leak at the hose joint or pump.

steps.title: Fill the coolant
steps.instruction: Fill with a 1:1 mix of ethylene-glycol antifreeze made for aluminium engines and distilled water. The full system takes about 1.03 L (1.09 US qt). Fill to the top, refit the cap, run the engine a few minutes, let it cool, then top up again.
verification: System full after the warm-up and cool-down.

steps.title: Fill the oil
steps.instruction: Add the amount that matches the engine: 1.20 L (1.27 US qt) after a full rebuild, 0.96 L (1.01 US qt) if only the filter was changed, 0.94 L (0.99 US qt) for an oil change. Use the oil grade listed in the break-in guide. Fit the filler cap with a new O-ring.

steps.title: Set chain slack
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel off the ground and the gearbox in neutral, set chain slack to 50–60 mm (1.97–2.36 in) with both adjusters turned equally. Tighten the rear axle nut to 135 N·m (100 lb·ft) and the adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft).
verification: Slack in range; axle and locknuts torqued.

steps.title: Go to the first-start guide
steps.instruction: Do not just start and ride: follow the first start and break-in guide for this bike for the oil flow check, leak checks and break-in.

entry_state: Engine removed from the frame, drained and clean on a bench.
exit_state: Head, valves, cylinder and piston measured, rebuilt and closed with timing and valve clearances checked; parts list recorded for break-in.
title: Top end teardown and rebuild: cylinder head, valves, cylinder and piston
completeness: Covers head cover, timing, camshafts with Plastigauge clearance, tensioner, head removal and warpage, valve leak test, valve, guide, spring and seat measurement, guide renewal and lapping, cylinder and piston measurement, rings, and reassembly with the angle-torque head bolt sequence.
excluded: Valve seat cutting (worn seats mean a new head)

required_tools.name: Torque wrench covering 6-40 N·m and an angle gauge
Valve guide remover, installer and 5.5 mm reamer (for guide renewal)
Micrometers, bore gauge, feeler gauges, straightedge, V-blocks and dial gauge
Molybdenum disulfide oil and grease, Yamaha bond No. 1215

required_parts.name: Head gasket, base gasket and head cover gasket
Valve stem seals
required_parts.purpose: Renewed whenever a valve is removed.

required_parts.name: Valves and guides, piston, rings, cylinder, cams

critical_stop_conditions: Valve seat pitted or contact width over limit: the head is replaced.
Bore over the wear limit or vertical scores: cylinder, piston and rings replaced together.
Cam marks not aligned after several turns: do not start; reset timing.
A cam cap clip or anything else dropped into the crankcase: recover it before going on.
Damaged head bolt threads in the crankcase: stop and repair.

steps.title: Set up on the bench
steps.instruction: Engine out, clean and on a bench support, oil and coolant drained. Lay out labelled trays so every lifter, pad and valve goes back where it came from.
verification: Clean engine on the bench, trays labelled.

steps.title: Remove the head cover
steps.instruction: Remove the spark plug. Remove the head cover bolts and lift off the cover with its gasket and the upper chain guide.

steps.title: Set top dead centre
steps.instruction: Remove the timing mark access screw and the crankshaft end access screw. Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise until the TDC mark on the rotor lines up with the mark on the cover; the mark on the exhaust cam sprocket and the mark on the intake cam sprocket must sit level with the top edge of the cylinder head. If not, turn one more turn.

steps.title: Remove the chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Remove the tensioner cap bolt, the tensioner bolts, the tensioner and its gaskets.

steps.title: Remove the camshafts
steps.instruction: Loosen the cam cap bolts a little at a time criss-cross from the outside in. Lift off the caps first so the two cap clips cannot drop into the crankcase, and take the clips out. Lift out the exhaust and intake cams and tie a wire to the timing chain.
verification: Cams and clips out, chain tied up.

steps.title: Inspect and measure the camshafts
steps.instruction: Look for blue marks, pitting or scratches on the lobes. Lobe height: intake standard 38.130–38.230 mm, limit 38.030 mm; exhaust standard 34.270–34.370 mm, limit 34.170 mm. Runout limit 0.030 mm (0.0012 in). Check cam-to-cap clearance with Plastigauge: cams in, strip on each journal, dowels and caps on, cap bolts tightened criss-cross from the inner caps out to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft) without turning the cams, then read the strip: intake 0.028–0.062 mm, exhaust 0.042–0.076 mm, limit 0.080 mm (0.0032 in). If out, measure the journal (intake 21.959–21.972 mm, exhaust 21.945–21.958 mm): journal out means a new cam, journal in spec means a new head and caps. Check the decompressor cam moves freely and its pin sticks out of the cam. More than 1/4 tooth worn on a sprocket, or a stiff chain, means cams and chain are replaced together.
verification: Lobe heights, runout and journal clearance recorded.

steps.title: Check the tensioner
steps.instruction: Wind the tensioner rod fully in clockwise with a thin screwdriver while pressing it lightly, then let go: it must push out smoothly. If not, or if cracked, replace it.

steps.title: Remove the cylinder head
steps.instruction: Loosen the head bolts half a turn at a time in sequence: the two M6 × 35 mm bolts, then the M10 bolts (three 149 mm long, one 165 mm long; note where the long one goes). Lift the head off and remove the intake chain guide, the head gasket and dowels.
verification: Head off, gasket out, bolt positions noted.

steps.title: Clean and check the head
steps.instruction: Scrape carbon from the chamber with a rounded scraper, protecting the plug threads. Clear the coolant passages. Measure warpage with a straightedge and feeler gauge: limit 0.05 mm (0.0020 in); if over, resurface on 400–600 grit wet paper on a flat plate with figure-eight strokes, turning the head as you go. Check the intake chain guide for wear.
verification: Warpage recorded; head and guide serviceable.

steps.title: Leak-test the valves
steps.instruction: Pour clean solvent into the intake and exhaust ports. Solvent seeping past a seat means that valve, seat and contact width need checking.

steps.title: Remove the valves
steps.instruction: Remove each lifter and pad in order (rag in the chain tunnel). Compress each spring with a valve spring compressor and attachment, remove the cotters, retainer, spring, valve, stem seal and spring seat, keeping each set with its position.

steps.title: Measure valves, guides and springs
steps.instruction: Stem diameter: intake standard 5.475–5.490 mm, limit 5.445 mm; exhaust standard 5.465–5.480 mm, limit 5.435 mm. Guide bore 5.500–5.512 mm. Stem-to-guide clearance (guide bore minus stem): intake standard 0.010–0.037 mm, limit 0.080 mm; exhaust standard 0.020–0.047 mm, limit 0.100 mm. Stem runout limit 0.010 mm (0.0004 in). Check stem ends for mushrooming. Spring free length: intake standard 40.57 mm, limit 38.54 mm; exhaust standard 37.42 mm, limit 35.55 mm. Spring tilt limit 1.8 mm (0.07 in) intake, 1.6 mm (0.06 in) exhaust. Check lifters for scratches (a damaged lifter means lifter and head are replaced).
verification: All valve, guide and spring readings recorded.

steps.title: Check the valve seats
steps.instruction: Clean carbon off faces and seats. Pitted or worn seats mean a new head. Coat the valve face with marking blue, press it onto the seat and measure the contact width: standard 0.90–1.10 mm, limit 1.5 mm (0.06 in). Out of limit means a new head.

branches.condition: Every measurement is inside its limit and the solvent test showed no leaks; the original valves and guides go back in.

steps.title: Renew valve guides if needed
steps.instruction: A new valve always gets a new guide. Heat the head to 100 °C (212 °F), drive the old guide out with the remover, and fit the new guide with the installer to a height of 15.1–15.5 mm (0.59–0.61 in) intake, 11.7–12.1 mm (0.46–0.48 in) exhaust. Ream it with the 5.5 mm reamer to get the stem clearance and reface the seat.

steps.title: Lap the seats
steps.instruction: The valves are titanium: lap with spare new valves and never fit a valve used for lapping. Coarse compound on the face (none in the guide), molybdenum disulfide oil on the stem, turn and tap until evenly polished, clean off, repeat with fine compound, clean off, then recheck the contact width with marking blue.
verification: Seat width in spec; lapping valves set aside.

steps.title: Fit the valves
steps.instruction: Clean the stem ends. Oil stems and new stem seals with molybdenum disulfide oil. Fit the spring seat, new stem seal, valve, spring (closer coils down) and retainer in each original position; compress the spring, fit the cotters and seat them with a light tap on the valve tip with a soft hammer. Oil and refit each pad and lifter in place; each lifter must turn freely.
verification: Valves fitted with new stem seals; lifters turn freely.

steps.title: Remove the cylinder and piston
steps.instruction: Remove the cylinder bolt and lift the cylinder off with its gasket and dowels. Rag in the crankcase, remove a pin clip, deburr the clip groove and push the pin out by hand (pin puller if stuck, never a hammer). Remove the piston and rings.

steps.title: Measure cylinder and piston
steps.instruction: Check walls for vertical scores. Bore 97.000–97.010 mm, wear limit 97.060 mm (3.8213 in), measured front-back and side-side at three heights. Piston 96.955–96.970 mm measured 9.0 mm up from the skirt bottom. Clearance 0.010–0.045 mm, limit 0.15 mm (0.006 in). Out of limit: cylinder, piston and rings replaced together.

steps.title: Measure rings and pin
steps.instruction: Clean the grooves. Ring side clearance: top 0.015–0.065 mm (limit 0.120 mm), 2nd 0.020–0.060 mm (limit 0.100 mm). Square each ring with the piston crown about 10 mm (0.39 in) up from the bottom of the bore and measure the end gap: top ring installed 0.20–0.30 mm, limit 0.55 mm; 2nd ring installed 0.35–0.50 mm, limit 0.85 mm. Pin outside diameter standard 17.991–18.000 mm, limit 17.971 mm; pin bore standard 18.004–18.015 mm, limit 18.045 mm. A blued or grooved pin means a new pin and a check of the oiling.

steps.title: Fit rings and piston
steps.instruction: Fit the oil ring expander, lower rail, upper rail, 2nd ring and top ring, maker marks up. Oil the pin with molybdenum disulfide oil. Fit the piston with its mark toward the exhaust (rear) side and new clips, clip ends away from the cutout, rag in the crankcase. Stagger the gaps: top ring and upper rail 15° either side of the intake centreline, 2nd ring and lower rail 15° either side of the exhaust centreline, expander 15° off the side axis; no two lined up.
verification: Piston on with new clips; gaps staggered.

steps.title: Fit the cylinder
steps.instruction: Oil piston, rings and bore. Fit a new base gasket and the dowels. Squeeze the rings and slide the cylinder down, passing the chain and exhaust chain guide through the tunnel. Cylinder bolt 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).

steps.title: Fit the head
steps.instruction: Pull the chain up and fit the intake chain guide, dowels, a new head gasket and the head. Clean the bolt threads, washers and crankcase threads, then put molybdenum disulfide grease on the bolt threads and seats and both faces of the washers.
verification: Head on; bolts and washers greased.

steps.title: Torque the head bolts
steps.instruction: Run the four M10 bolts in sequence to 40 N·m (30 lb·ft) in two or three stages. Remove them, re-grease threads, seats and washers, and refit them in sequence to 22 N·m (16 lb·ft). Mark each bolt head and the head, turn every bolt 90° in sequence, then give the three 149 mm bolts a further 60° and the 165 mm bolt a further 90°. Tighten the two M6 bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: M10: 40 N·m, then 22 N·m + 90° + (60° short / 90° long); M6 10 N·m.

steps.title: Fit the camshafts
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise to TDC. Coat the cams with molybdenum disulfide oil and oil the decompressor. Fill the head with engine oil up to the tops of the lifters. Fit the chain over both sprockets and drop the cams in with the marks aligned as at removal. Do not turn the crankshaft now. Cover the head with a rag, fit the two clips and the caps, and tighten the oiled cap bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft) in two or three stages in sequence.
verification: Cams in on the marks; clips fitted; caps 10 N·m.

steps.title: Fit the tensioner
steps.instruction: Wind the rod fully in and hold it. With the UP mark facing up fit the gasket, tensioner and gasket and tighten its bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Release the rod, check it pushes out, and fit the cap bolt with its gasket at 6 N·m (4.4 lb·ft).

steps.title: Check the timing
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise several turns by hand. At TDC the rotor mark and cam marks must line up again; if not, reset the cams. Check cold valve clearances: intake 0.10–0.17 mm, exhaust 0.15–0.22 mm, and change pads as needed.

steps.title: Close the head
steps.instruction: Fit the upper chain guide. Fit a new head cover gasket with a thin coat of Yamaha bond No. 1215 on it. After fitting the new gasket to the cover, trim off its marked tab section. Fit the cover and tighten its bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Fit the breather hose and the spark plug at 13 N·m (9.6 lb·ft). Refit the access screws: timing mark screw 6 N·m (4.4 lb·ft), crankshaft end screw 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: Cover 10 N·m; plug 13 N·m; access screws torqued.

steps.title: Record the top end and move on
steps.instruction: Record the parts replaced (they decide the break-in). Refit the engine with the engine out and in guide and follow the first start and break-in guide.

Then one bolt at a time in sequence: remove only that bolt, re-grease it and its washer, refit to 18 N·m (13 lb·ft), mark it and turn it a further 90°, before moving to the next. When all four are done, turn each a further 60° in sequence (150° total). Finally tighten the two M6 bolts to 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft) with threadlocker.
verification: Each M10 bolt: 18 N·m + 90° + 60°; M6 bolts 12 N·m.

steps.title: Fit the camshafts
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise to TDC. Coat the cams with molybdenum disulfide oil and oil the decompressor. Fit the chain over both sprockets and drop the exhaust and intake cams in with the sprocket marks level with the cap faces. Do not turn the crankshaft now. Fit the caps and tighten the cap bolts (oiled threads and faces) to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft) in two or three stages in sequence.
verification: Cams in on the marks; cap bolts 10 N·m in sequence.

steps.title: Fit the tensioner
steps.instruction: Wind the tensioner rod fully in and hold it. With the UP mark facing up fit the gasket, tensioner and gasket and tighten its two bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Release the rod, check it pushes out, and fit the cap bolt with its gasket at 6 N·m (4.4 lb·ft).

steps.title: Check the timing
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise several turns by hand. At TDC the rotor mark and the cam sprocket marks must line up again. If not, go back and reset the cams. Then check the cold valve clearances: intake 0.10–0.17 mm, exhaust 0.15–0.22 mm, and change pads as needed.
verification: Timing marks align after several turns; clearances recorded.

steps.title: Close the head
steps.instruction: Fit the upper chain guide. Coat the new head cover gasket with Three Bond 1541C sealant, fit it with a new plug hole gasket, and fit the cover. Tighten the cover bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Fit the breather hose and the spark plug at 13 N·m (9.6 lb·ft). Refit both access screws: timing mark screw 6 N·m (4.4 lb·ft), crankshaft end screw 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft), with oiled O-rings.
verification: Cover 10 N·m; plug 13 N·m; access screws torqued.

steps.title: Record the top end and move on
steps.instruction: Record the parts replaced (they decide the break-in). Refit the engine with the engine out and in guide, then follow the first start and break-in guide.

steps.title: Start with a stripped top end
steps.instruction: Engine out on the bench, oil and coolant drained, head, cylinder and piston removed (top end guide). Cover the crankcase mouth.

steps.title: Remove the left cover and AC magneto rotor
steps.instruction: Mark and remove the shift pedal. Remove the left crankcase cover bolts, cover, gasket and dowels. Hold the rotor, remove the nut and washer, pull the AC magneto rotor with a rotor puller and remove the woodruff key. Remove the stator and pickup if they need renewing.

steps.title: Remove the starter motor
steps.instruction: Remove the starter motor cover and bolts and pull the starter out.

steps.title: Remove the clutch
steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover and O-ring. Undo the six clutch spring bolts criss-cross and remove the springs, pressure plate, push rod 1 with its circlip, washer and bearing, the ball and push rod 2. Remove the plates in order. Hold the boss with a universal clutch holder and remove the boss nut, conical washer and washer, then the clutch boss, thrust washer, primary driven gear and push lever shaft.

steps.title: Measure the clutch
steps.instruction: Friction plates 2.92–3.08 mm, wear limit 2.82 mm (measure at four points; replace as a set). Clutch plate warpage limit 0.10 mm (replace as a set). Clutch spring free length 48.00 mm, limit 45.60 mm (replace as a set). Push rod 2 bend limit 0.10 mm. Check housing dogs and boss splines for pitting, the pressure plate for cracks and the push lever shaft for wear.

steps.title: Remove the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and element, radiator pipe 2, then the right crankcase cover bolts, cover, gasket, dowels and collar.

steps.title: Remove and check the starter clutch
steps.instruction: Remove the starter clutch holder (3 bolts), washer, damper and starter clutch. Fit the drive gear onto the starter clutch: it must turn freely counterclockwise and lock clockwise. Check gears for chips or wear.
verification: Starter clutch locks one way only.

steps.title: Remove the balancer and primary gears
steps.instruction: Flatten the lock washer tabs. Wedge an aluminium plate between the balancer drive and weight gears and loosen the balancer nut, the primary drive gear nut and the balancer weight gear nut. Remove the balancer, straight key, conical washer, primary drive gear, balancer drive gear, lock washers and balancer weight gear. Check the balancer for cracks and the gears for wear.

steps.title: Remove and check the oil pump
steps.instruction: Remove the oil pump bolts and the pump. Strip it: cover, outer rotor, dowel, inner rotor, drive shaft and housing. Measure inner-to-outer rotor tip clearance 0.000–0.150 mm; housing-to-rotor side clearance 0.06–0.11 mm, limit 0.18 mm; out of limit means a new pump.

steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Pull the shift shaft with its spring, collar and roller. Remove the shift guide bolts and take the shift guide and shift lever assembly off together. Turn the segment counterclockwise to its stop and remove its bolt without knocking the stopper lever; remove segment, stopper lever, collar and spring.

steps.title: Remove the timing chain
steps.instruction: Remove the exhaust chain guide, its stopper plate and the timing chain.

steps.title: Split the crankcases
steps.instruction: Lay the engine left side down. Loosen the twelve case bolts (five 45 mm, four 60 mm, three 75 mm) a quarter turn at a time criss-cross and remove them. Lever only at the splitting slots and tap the reinforced bosses with a soft hammer; lift the right case off evenly, leaving the crank and gearbox in the left case. If it sticks, find the missed fastener; never force it.

steps.title: Remove the gearbox
steps.instruction: Note where each shift fork sits and which way it faces. Remove the guide bars and springs, the shift cam and forks 3, 2 and 1, then tap the drive axle lightly and lift both axles out together. Remove the collar.

steps.title: Remove the crank and balancer shaft
steps.instruction: Lift the balancer shaft out with its flat side toward the crank. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool.

steps.title: Measure the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Runout limit 0.030 mm (0.0012 in), turning slowly. Crank width 61.93–62.00 mm (2.438–2.441 in). Big-end side clearance 0.150–0.450 mm (0.0059–0.0177 in); out of range means the big-end bearing, crank pin or rod is worn. Check the crank sprocket and blow out the journal oil passage. A crank out of limit is replaced; connecting rod and big-end rebuild is not covered here.

steps.title: Inspect the gearbox
steps.instruction: Main and drive axle runout limit 0.08 mm (0.0032 in). Check gears for blueing, pitting or wear and dogs for cracks or rounded edges, and that every gear slides freely. Roll the guide bars on a flat surface (bent bars replaced, never straightened). Check fork followers and pawls, fork movement on the bars, and the shift cam grooves and segment.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the cases
steps.instruction: Wash the cases, remove all old sealant, blow out the oil passages and check for cracks. Turn each case bearing by hand; a rough or loose one is pressed out by its inner race (never reused) and a new one pressed in by its outer race. Refit the bearing cover plates with threadlocker: crank bearing plate screws 22 N·m (16 lb·ft), other plate bolts 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft). Fit a new left case oil seal 0–0.5 mm deep.
verification: Cases clean; bearings and seals checked or renewed.

steps.title: Fit the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Grease the seal lips with lithium-soap grease and coat the journals with molybdenum disulfide grease. Pull the crank into the left case bearing with the crankshaft installer pot, bolt, M12 adapter and spacer, holding the rod at TDC, until it bottoms. Fit the balancer shaft.

steps.title: Build and fit the gearbox
steps.instruction: Main axle: 5th pinion (21T), 3rd (20T), collar, 4th (22T), 2nd (15T). Drive axle: collar, 2nd wheel (23T), 4th (24T), 3rd (26T), 5th (20T), collar, 1st (27T), new O-ring; washer and new circlip with its sharp edge away from the gear and ends on a spline crest. Molybdenum disulfide oil on idler and sliding gear bores. Fit the collar past the seal lip, drop both axles in together, then fork 1 (L) into 4th wheel, fork 3 (R) into 5th wheel, fork 2 (C) into 3rd pinion, the shift cam, the guide bars and springs. Oil everything and check every gear selects.

steps.title: Close the crankcases
steps.instruction: Fit the oil nozzle with threadlocker at 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft), the dowels and a greased O-ring, and apply Yamaha bond No. 1215 to the mating face. Lower the right case on with the rod at TDC, tapping gently. Tighten the twelve case bolts in two stages criss-cross to 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft). Crank and gearbox must turn freely.
verification: Cases closed at 12 N·m; everything turns freely.

steps.title: Fit the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and lever with threadlocker on its bolt at 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). With the lever pushed down, fit the segment with its notch on the shift cam pin, oil the bolt shank and tighten to 30 N·m (22 lb·ft) without knocking the lever. Oil and assemble the pawls, pins and springs into the shift lever, fit it together with the shift guide and tighten the guide bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft) with threadlocker. Fit the oiled roller, spring, collar and shift shaft and a new shaft oil seal.
verification: Shift parts torqued; gears change by hand.

steps.title: Fit the timing chain
steps.instruction: Fit the timing chain over the crank sprocket and the exhaust chain guide with its stopper plate at 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft) with threadlocker.

steps.title: Fit the oil pump
steps.instruction: Oil the drive shaft and inner rotor, fit the dowel in the inner rotor groove, the oiled outer rotor and the cover with its screw at 2.0 N·m (1.5 lb·ft). Fit the pump with threadlocker on its bolts at 5 N·m (3.7 lb·ft). It must turn smoothly.

steps.title: Fit the balancer and primary gears
steps.instruction: Fit the balancer weight gear with its lower spline on the balancer shaft lower spline. Fit the balancer drive gear with its punch mark on the weight gear punch mark and its lower spline on the crank lower spline. Fit a new lock washer and the weight gear nut at 50 N·m (37 lb·ft). Fit the primary drive gear, a new conical washer (convex side out) and the oiled primary drive gear nut at 80 N·m (59 lb·ft), with an aluminium plate wedging the gears. Fit the straight key, the balancer, a new lock washer and the balancer nut at 45 N·m (33 lb·ft). Bend the lock washer tabs.

steps.title: Refit the starter clutch
steps.instruction: Fit the starter clutch, damper, washer and holder; holder bolts with threadlocker at 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft).

steps.title: Fit the right cover
steps.instruction: Fit a new cover oil seal (marks inward, greased lip), the washer and a new circlip. Fit the dowels, greased new O-rings, the collar and a new gasket. Refit radiator pipe 2 (joint bolt 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft)), a new oil filter element and the filter cover at 10 N·m.
verification: Right cover 10 N·m; impeller engaged; new filter.

steps.title: Rebuild the clutch
steps.instruction: Fit the push lever shaft (greased seal lip, oiled sliding surface). Fit the oiled primary driven gear, thrust washer and clutch boss. Fit the washer, a new conical washer (convex side out) and the oiled boss nut; hold the boss with the universal clutch holder and tighten to 90 N·m (66 lb·ft). Fit the oiled plates starting and ending with a friction plate, from the boss side: three friction plates 1, three purple-marked friction plates 2, then two friction plates 1, with a clutch plate between each. Fit the bearing, washer and a new circlip on push rod 1, then oiled push rod 2, the ball and push rod 1. Fit the pressure plate, springs and spring bolts in stages criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Fit a greased new cover O-ring and the clutch cover at 10 N·m.
verification: Plate order correct; spring bolts and cover 10 N·m.

steps.title: Fit the stator and AC magneto rotor
steps.instruction: Fit the stator with threadlocker on its screws at 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft) (T25 bit), the crank position sensor bolts at 10 N·m with threadlocker and the lead holder bolt at 8 N·m (5.9 lb·ft) with threadlocker; seal the lead grommet with Yamaha bond No. 1215. Clean the tapers, fit the woodruff key flat side parallel to the crank, the rotor, washer and nut at 65 N·m (48 lb·ft). Fit dowels, a new gasket, the cover and lead holder with the bolts criss-cross at 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).

steps.title: Refit the starter motor
steps.instruction: Grease the starter O-ring, refit the starter and cover: starter bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft), cover bolt 10 N·m.

steps.title: Final hand check
steps.instruction: Turn the crank by hand through several turns in neutral and in each gear: smooth, no tight spots.
verification: Engine turns freely; all gears select.

steps.title: Continue with the top end
steps.instruction: Build the top end with the top end guide, refit the engine, fill with 0.90 L (0.95 US qt) of oil and follow the first start and break-in guide. A new crankshaft or gears means the full break-in.
